land.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

successors.note: The Crotone page: 'What was left of its population submitted to Rome in 277 BC'; 'In 194 BC, it became the site of a Roman colony.' Before that the city was occupied by Dionysius I (379-367), by Agathocles (295, end bridged to 289, his death) and by the Bruttii (undated on the page, bridged 289-277).

capitals.name: Croton (Crotone)
capitals.note: Gulf of Crotone, Calabria; walls of 'twelve miles (19 km)' at the time of Pyrrhus.

correction.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Croton. The Crotone page gives a city area of 'at least 617 hectares' and the modern comune (179.8 km2), no km2 for the chora; the province of Crotone (1,264 km2, the gazetteer) is a reading of the polis territory. 'Croton ... expanded its influence over the Bruttian peninsula founding possibly Caulonia' (later 7th century; 'possibly', so not drawn).

correction.text: Croton and the confederation of Sybaris's 25 cities

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Sybaris's fall 'Croton became the capital of a confederation including the 25 city-states in the region of Sybaris' (coins c. 480-460). The province of Cosenza stands for the 25 cities as in the sybaris dossier. Ends in 445: the Sybaris page has the Krotoniates drive the refounded Sybaris out in 446/445 and Thurii founded on the site in 444/443, and the confederation is not recorded after the coins of 460 (see the -444 loss). The Italiote League (founded 'about 430', Croton its first leader, Taras after 379; Italiote League page) is an alliance and not drawn.

correction.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Croton alone, once the Sybarite region passes to Thurii ('In 444/443 BC the Athenians and other new colonists then turned the city into a new foundation called Thurii'). The Crotone page names no end for the confederation and no later extent; the Sybaris page does not say what became of the 25 cities, so the loss of the province of Cosenza is the researcher's reading, dated by Thurii. Croton stays hegemon of the Italiote League until Dionysius takes it in 379 (Italiote League page), an alliance not drawn.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: independence regained after twelve years (379 + 12); the page does not say what became of the confederation.

correction.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 295 BC, Croton fell to another Syracusan tyrant, Agathocles'; later 'occupied by the Bruttii, with the exception of the citadel' (undated) and 'after the Pyrrhic War, half the town was deserted'. Held as the city's territory until 277; the occupier is Syracuse to 289 (Agathocles's death, bridge) and the Bruttii from 289 (bridge), both hatched.

ledger.note: 710: the Achaeans found Croton. The ancient colony 'was thought to be 710 BC'; Myscellus 'made three founding expeditions', the third around 708 BC. The page names the colony and the date; the land (province of Crotone) is a reading.

region.text: the region of Sybaris and its 25 city-states

ledger.note: 510: Croton destroys Sybaris and heads its region. 'Croton sent an army of 100,000 men commanded by the wrestler Milo against Sybaris and destroyed it'; 'Croton became the capital of a confederation including the 25 city-states in the region of Sybaris' (coins c. 480-460). The page dates only the crisis to 510.

region.text: the region of Sybaris and its 25 city-states

ledger.note: 444: the Sybarite land passes to Thurii. 'In 444/443 BC the Athenians and other new colonists then turned the city into a new foundation called Thurii' (after the Krotoniates drove the Sybarites out of their refounded city in 446/445). The year is the page's; that Croton's authority over the 25 cities ends with it is the researcher's reading (the page is silent on the 25 cities, and the Crotone page gives the confederation only by coins of 480-460).

ledger.note: 379: Dionysius I of Syracuse takes Croton. Dionysius 'captured Croton in 379 BC and held it for twelve years'.

ledger.note: 367: Croton is free again. The page gives the twelve-year duration (379 + 12 = 367), not the end year.

ledger.note: 295: Agathocles takes Croton. 'In 295 BC, Croton fell to another Syracusan tyrant, Agathocles.'

region.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

ledger.note: 289: the Syracusan hold on Croton ends with Agathocles's death. The Crotone page dates no end ('In 295 BC, Croton fell to another Syracusan tyrant, Agathocles'); the Agathocles page gives his death in 289 BC and says nothing of Croton in 295 or of his Italian possessions afterwards; -289 is a bridge, the latest the Syracusan hold can have lasted.

region.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

ledger.note: 289: the Bruttii hold Croton, 'with the exception of the citadel'. The Crotone page: 'Croton was then occupied by the Bruttii, with the exception of the citadel' (undated; before 'the Pyrrhic War, half the town was deserted'); the Bruttii page dates their rise to about 356 and says nothing of Croton. Start bridged to Agathocles's death.

region.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

ledger.note: 277: the Bruttian occupation ends with the submission to Rome. The page dates no end ('What was left of its population submitted to Rome in 277 BC'); bridged to that year.

ledger.note: 277: Croton submits to Rome. 'What was left of its population submitted to Rome in 277 BC'; 'after the Pyrrhic War, half the town was deserted'.

wars.name: Battle of the Sagra
wars.outcome: 'The victory of Locri and Rhegium over Croton in the battle of the Sagra in middle of the sixth century BC interrupted the expansion of the city.'
wars.note: The page dates it only to the middle of the sixth century; the years here are a span.

wars.name: Kroton-Sybaris war
wars.outcome: Croton destroyed Sybaris and headed a confederation of 25 city-states.
wars.note: The page dates the crisis to 510 and gives no precise date for the destruction.

wars.name: Syracusan conquests of Croton

zones.text: Croton and its territory: the province of Crotone (1,264 km2) as the chora

wars.outcome: Dionysius I held Croton from 379 for twelve years; Agathocles took it in 295 and the hold is bridged to his death in 289.
wars.note: The Italiote League was founded 'to defend itself from the expansionist aims of Syracuse', with Croton as hegemon (undated on the Crotone page; 'about 430' on the Italiote League page, which has Taras take the lead after 379). The Agathocles page reports no capture of Croton in 295.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier of Croton; the chora and the Sybarite confederation are approximate.

sources.title: Agathocles of Syracuse
sources.note: Death in 289 BC (bridge for the end of the Syracusan hold); the page mentions Croton only for an early defence against the Bruttii and a failed attempt to take it, and reports no capture in 295.

sources.title: Bruttii
sources.note: Rise about 356 BC, league with Consentia as capital, occupation of Hipponium, Terina and Thurii (undated); no mention of an occupation of Croton.

sources.title: Italiote League
sources.note: Founded about 430 BC, Croton first leader, Taras after Dionysius took Croton in 379, existing until at least 278; names no 25-city confederation and no extent.

notes: The Kroton page is a disambiguation page (opened first, no history); the history is on Crotone. Territory is a reading: province of Crotone (chora), plus the province of Cosenza for the 25-city confederation. The page does not date the end of the Syracusan and Bruttian occupations; -277 is a bridge (confidence 1). 'Croton' is also called 'Kroton'. Terina (founded 480-470, 'on the Tyrrhenian coast') and Caulonia ('possibly') are colonies, not drawn; Croton belonged to the Italiote League (hegemon). Gazetteer names used that it lacks: none beyond the admin-1 spellings Natural Earth uses ('Crotene'). Repair of 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): the Sybarite province (Cosenza) is lost at 444 to Thurii (Sybaris page, 444/443; confidence 2, the fate of the 25 cities is not on the page) and a new keyframe -444..-380 shows Croton alone; the end of the Syracusan hold is bridged to Agathocles's death in 289 (confidence 1; the Agathocles page gives 289 but reports no capture of Croton in 295, which only the Crotone page has) and the Bruttii hold the city 289-277 (confidence 1; undated on the Crotone page, whose 'then' follows the Syracusan sentence). The Bruttii page does not mention Croton; the Italiote League page names no confederation of 25 cities.
